messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Bridgewater rollout dependency: prioritized feature request

Hi Markus / Monica,

Quick context: Bridgewater (Emily Chen) has a hard go-live target for their Q4 rollout and the deal is contingent on two things we currently don't have in GA: deterministic tenant-model affinity (routing pinning) and tenant-level KM-enforced keying for inference logs. They want a single-point SLA for latency (p95 < 120ms) and a deterministic routing guarantee so their compliance team can sign off.

Attached: Bridgewater_SOW_v2.pdf and a short requirements brief (bridgewater_prod_requirements.md). HubSpot link: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/BW-2026-Q4-01.

Ask: can Eng prioritize a scoped change that provides a model-affinity pin (config flag + routing order) plus a lightweight audit hook (minimal logging + KMS envelope metadata) for the Bridgewater tenant in the next two sprints?

What I need from you by EOD tomorrow:
- high-level feasibility (yes/no)
- rough effort (story points or sprints)
- any non-negotiable dependencies (infra, security sign-offs, KMS work)

What Bridgewater is offering in return: a signed 12-month Dedicated commitment (deal BW-2026-Q4-01) and willingness to accept an initial GA with limited model variants if we provide documented fallback behavior + monitoring. Procurement timeline is tight — procurement@bridgewater.com asked for a final SOW + delivery plan by next Friday.

This is high impact (enterprise logo + reference) — appreciate a candid assessment. If this is a hard blocker, we should escalate to product leadership.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: Bridgewater rollout dependency: prioritized feature request

Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the docs. Quick read: promising but has a few technical risks.

On Sun, Nov 29, 2026 at 09:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick context: Bridgewater (Emily Chen) has a hard go-live target for their Q4 rollout and the deal is contingent on two things we currently don't have in GA: deterministic tenant-model affinity (routing pinning) and tenant-level KM-enforced keying for inference logs.

Comments / questions:
- Deterministic affinity: we can implement a "pinning" configuration that ties tenant -> model_variant preference in the routing layer, but guaranteeing absolute determinism under autoscale (preemption, node loss) requires state persistence or sticky sessions. That adds complexity to our runtime and changes how KV cache is sharded.
- KMS-enforced keying: if Bridgewater needs HSM-backed envelopes and per-tenant key rotation, that's a security integration (KMS + customer-managed CMK) and will require security review + vault changes. How strict is their requirement? Is per-request envelope mandatory or is metadata-only acceptable initially?

Estimate (very rough): scoped affinity + config flag + fallback policy + minimal audit hook = ~2 sprints for core runtime changes + 1 sprint integration/QA assuming no infra blockers. If we need strong persistence (sticky state across shards) add another 1-2 sprints.

Workaround proposal (short-term): we can offer a semi-deterministic staging plan: 1) reserve dedicated capacity for Bridgewater (Dedicated pool) and enforce model_variant on the load balancer; 2) provide documented fallback behavior and enhanced telemetry dashboards. This reduces runtime changes but increases cost (and requires Dedicated infra commit).

I've created JIRA ticket ENG-7890 to track the engineering work. I'll add acceptance criteria and link the SOW.

Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Inference Platform Engineering

Adding customer context from my call with Emily earlier today.

On Sun, Nov 29, 2026 at 11:05 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Estimate (very rough): scoped affinity + config flag + fallback policy + minimal audit hook = ~2 sprints for core runtime changes + 1 sprint integration/QA ...

Emily's clarifications:
- Go-live hard date: Bridgewater's pilot must be live by 2027-01-20. They understand a phased rollout (limited model variants okay) but procurement requires a concrete delivery plan.
- Security stance: they'd prefer per-request customer-managed CMK for log envelopes, but they said "we can accept per-batch metadata linking to their KMS key for the pilot" if it speeds delivery.
- Budget/commitment: they're prepared to sign a 12-month Dedicated contract if we can commit to a phased delivery plan; procurement will push DocuSign once SOW + delivery milestones are confirmed. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/bridgewater-sow-v2

Negotiation levers I can use: 1) offer a 6-month discounted Dedicated rate during ramp if Eng can commit to the 2-sprint scoped delivery; 2) make the initial GA model-variant-limited with explicit fallback docs + SLA addendum.

Attachment: customer email excerpt (redacted) and SOW draft.

Monica

Customer Success Manager — Strategic Accounts

Thanks both — helpful. Summarizing and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Decision points / asks for Eng (Markus):
1) Feasibility: confirm by EOD tomorrow if the scoped change (pinning config + minimal audit hook with metadata-only KMS linkage) is acceptable as a Phase 1 deliverable.
2) Effort: add a concrete estimate into ENG-7890 and flag any required security sign-offs.
3) Fallback path: if full determinism requires >2 sprints, recommend whether we should 1) take Dedicated pool + LB-enforced variant for pilot or 2) delay go-live.

Customer commitments provided:
- Bridgewater will sign the 12-month Dedicated contract (deal BW-2026-Q4-01) contingent on the delivery plan.
- Procurement expects an updated SOW and milestone schedule by next Friday.

Acceptance criteria for Phase 1 (what we promise them):
- Tenant can set a model_variant preference via config and routing honors it for >=95% of requests under normal operation.
- Audit metadata includes a linkable KMS key id and request UUID for Bridgewater (per-batch acceptable).
- Monitoring dashboard with p95 latency and a fallback-runbook linked in the SOW.

If Eng can confirm the scoped approach, I'll lock the SOW and get DocuSign started (Monica, please hold any pricing levers until I confirm). If not, tell me ASAP so I can manage expectations with Emily and procurement.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:00 AM PST if that helps — invite to follow.

Laura
